summary: Consciousness's ZX Spectrum Enhanced demo, which won the Enhanced 8-Bit Demo compo at DiHalt 2015. Code is by VBI and Rob F., with music by nq and graphics by Nodeus, Mellona and Brightentayle.
why: A compo winner on the enhanced Spectrum, tagged ts-conf, with a three-person graphics team and NQ/Skrju appearing as a guest artist.

summary: Metalvotze's demo for the Vectrex, which won the Alternative Demo/Intro compo at Buenzli 2008.
why: A compo winner for the Vectrex. It's tagged nsfw, so mind where you watch it. The source was once available, but the links were down as of 2021.

summary: Fairlight's story-driven C64 demo, third in the C64 Demo compo at Little Computer People 2005. Hollowman did the code, graphics and concept, with music by Goto80. Nominated for two Scene.org Awards in 2005.
why: Sceners call it eerie, nauseating and coherent, and it grows on people over repeat viewings. One calls it the best story-based demo on the C64.

quote.text: This is the best story based demo on the C64. I always liked both themed and story based demos and wished there were more of them.

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC from Logon System, with code by Overflow and music by McKlain.
why: A small, size-limited CPC production. The fact sheet has little else to go on, so the video will tell you more than we can.

summary: New Generation, Zelax and Radiance's Atari 8-bit demo, first in the Demo compo at Lost Party 2024. The video here is captured on real hardware.
why: A compo winner with a cyberpunk, Blade Runner-themed look and a synthwave soundtrack, tagged for the Meteoriks 2025 watchlist. It needs 1 MB of memory.

summary: Reflex's C64 demo, first in the Wild compo at Gubbdata 2021. Quiss did the code, with music by kb and PVCF and graphics by Felidae. Commenters describe the 1541 disk drive producing the video signal.
why: Won Outstanding Concept and Outstanding Technical Achievement at the Meteoriks 2022. Sceners keep coming back to the sheer cleverness of using the drive itself, music included.

quote.text: this is what the scene is about for me, doing something 'impossible'.

summary: Booze Design and Instinct's C64 demo, third in the C64 Demo compo at X 2010 and nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the 2010 Scene.org Awards. Code by HCL, JackAsser and Dane, graphics by Archmage.
why: Sceners single out the isometric voxel routine, the huge rotozoomer that reaches into the borders, and the smooth transitions. Some thought it deserved to win the compo.

quote.text: Excellent in every aspect, fantastic code, supersmooth design and transitions and beautiful graphics etc.

summary: Lamers' Atari 8-bit demo, first in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k12. Code by Ajcek, Alias and Szeryf, with graphics by At0m and Gepard and music by Wieczór.
why: A compo winner, with a three-person code team. Little else is on record, so the video is the best guide.

summary: A 4K intro for the ZX Spectrum by SerzhSoft and Gasman, first in the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2019. SerzhSoft did code and graphics, Gasman the music. This is the party version.
why: Nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement and Best Low-End Production at the Meteoriks 2020. A full intro, music included, in 4096 bytes on a Spectrum.

summary: LaResistance's Atari 8-bit demo, first in the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2007. Pr0be did the code, Powrooz the graphics, and Born the music and the 3D objects.
why: A compo winner. Born's credit includes 3D objects, which is the thing to look for here.

summary: Arise's C64 demo, second in the C64 Demo compo at Moonshine Dragons 2022. It uses the Sparkle loader. Code by Luke and Wacek, with music by Jammer and Rodney and graphics by Rodney, Wacek, Biter and Bimber.
why: Won Best Oldschool Production at the Meteoriks 2023. Commenters praise the design and surprises, and argue over how much is precalculated animation and how much is real-time code.

quote.text: Wacek and the Arise team never disappoints. The amount of determination, talent and work that went into this demo is paramount.

summary: Bonzai's C64 demo that won the Demo compo at X 2016. It spans two disk sides, with code by Trap, Walt and Ricky and music by DRAX, Laxity, Metal and Scortia.
why: It opened the compo and went down very well with the crowd, and sceners welcomed it as a comeback. They single out the sinewave zoom scroller, the Star Wars-style upscroll and the transitions.

quote.text: I love the way how this combines oldschool vibes with perfect sync and transitions.

summary: Inward and Cyberpunks Unity's ZX Spectrum demo, third in the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2007. This is the first part of a two-part title.
why: A podium finish in a Breakpoint wild compo. The fact sheet is thin, so the video is the best way in.

summary: The Next Level is a VIC-20 demo by Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2008. Viznut did the code, graphics and music.
why: Nominated for Most Original Concept and Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the 2008 Scene.org Awards. It's tagged for speech synthesis, which is the thing to listen for.

summary: Ate Bit's demo for the ZX Spectrum 128, first in the Open Oldschool Demo compo at Sundown 2007. evilpaul did the code and graphics, with music by 4mat.
why: A compo winner for the 128K Spectrum, made by a two-person team.

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo, first in the C64 Demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2001. HCL did the code and graphics, with three more graphics artists and seven musicians credited. This entry is tagged as the party version.
why: It wasn't released at the party because of bugs; a final version followed in November at X2001. Commenters point people to that bug-fixed release.

summary: Lamers' Atari 8-bit demo, second in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k16. Code by Ajcek and Szeryf, graphics by Gepard, Johny, Odyn1ec and At0m, music by XTD. The video is the party version at 1080p50.
why: A runner-up from the same team that won the XL/XE compo at Silly Venture 2k12 with Boogie Nights.

summary: Byterapers' C64 demo, second in the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2009. Suckho did the code and graphics, with music by GRG. It's tagged as an endless loop.
why: Commenters like the soundtrack and the smooth twisters, and were surprised by how good the 8x8 plasma looks. One notes it as Suckho's first C64 release.

quote.text: The rest of the demo was great, twisters looked so smooth and who knew 8x8 plasma could look so good.

summary: A co-op between Censor Design and Oxyron: a two-sided C64 demo that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2015. It uses the Bitbreaker loader and has a large team of coders, artists and musicians.
why: Nominated for three Meteoriks in 2016. Sceners praise the bitmap stretchers added to the effects, Joe's graphics and the music, and describe side 2 as a music-driven piece.

quote.text: Really powerful demo with great coding, gfx and music.

summary: Agenda's Atari 8-bit demo, second in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k14. Probe did the code, with graphics by Ooz, Piesiu and Ripek and music by stRing. It's tagged 128k.
why: A runner-up at Silly Venture. Little else is on record, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Battro is a 16K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Batman Group, with code by Rhino, music by McKlain and graphics by Mac.
why: A compact CPC production in the 16K size class. The fact sheet has no placings or comments, so there is not much more to add.

summary: Oxyron's C64 demo, second in the C64 Demo compo at Breakpoint 2007. Graham and Axis did the code, Yazoo the graphics and Fanta the music, with Koala pictures by Oyise at the end.
why: Sceners welcomed it as Oxyron's return, and several named it their favourite of the Breakpoint compo. They single out the design, the graphics, the vectors and the music.

quote.text: Smooth routines and especially the music had some suprising elements.

summary: Noice's demo for the ZX Spectrum 128, second in the Old School Executable Demo compo at Sundown 2012. Shadow did the code, Frost the graphics and Yerzmyey the music.
why: A runner-up at Sundown with a music credit for Yerzmyey. Little else is on record.

summary: Lepsi and Miracles' C64 demo that won the Demo compo at Silesia 5 in 2011, nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards. It uses the Krill loader and features Joodas's fullscreen picture Sprocket.
why: Commenters call it original and well made, with high-quality graphics that fit the effects, and some count it among the best demos they've seen. They single out the x-rotators and the soundtrack.

quote.text: Excellent gfx and code, great soundtrack (especially Apparatus.sid!).

summary: deMarche's ZX Spectrum demo, first in the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2016. TmK did the code, Rainman and bfox the graphics, Nik-O the music and Zeebr the direction. The source is available.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Demo at the Meteoriks 2017. The video is a full-resolution, no-flicker 50Hz capture, and the demo carries a graffiti tag.

summary: Logicoma's 4K intro for the C64, second in the Combined Intro compo at Solskogen 2017. Ferris did the code and graphics, H0ffman the music, 4mat the sound driver and Wobble more graphics. The source is public.
why: Sceners were pleased to see Logicoma on the C64 and noted it as Ferris's first C64 prod. One hears EDM vibes in the bass notes and arpeggios of the tune.

quote.text: super nice 4k intro, and especially since it's your first one!!!

summary: Mahoney's C64 demo, fourth in the C64 Demo compo at X 2010 and nominated for Best Technical Achievement at the 2010 Scene.org Awards. It processes audio in real time, and a white paper explains how.
why: Sceners were stunned that a 1MHz machine can time-stretch sound live, and some call it the best work on the C64 so far. Several also single out the accompanying white paper.

quote.text: Real time timestretching on a 1mhz machine? You gotta be kidding.

summary: Darklite and Offence's ZX Spectrum 128 demo that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2023. Neon did the code, Pal the graphics and Response the music. It uses the ZX multicolour mode.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at the Meteoriks 2024, so worth a look for what the multicolour mode makes possible on the Spectrum.

summary: A monochrome Atari 8-bit demo by Masters of Electric City and Checkpoint, third in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k14. bob_er did the code, mOdmate the graphics and Dhor the music.
why: A podium finish that sticks to a single-colour look. The video is a 720p, 50fps capture.

summary: Phantasy's Game Boy demo, fifth in the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2005. Dalton and Lai wrote the code, Exocet did the graphics, and Goto80 and Mr. Death made the music.
why: A Game Boy demo with a chess part and a plasma part. Several parts rely on interlacing, so screenshots don't show them as they look in motion.

summary: Techno Lab's ZX Spectrum demo, third in the 8bit Demo compo at Multimatograf 2018. Kowalski did the code and Nik-O the music, with tools and support from wbcbz7.
why: A podium finish at Multimatograf. The fact sheet is thin, so the video is the best guide.

summary: deMarche's ZX Spectrum 128K demo, first in the ZX Spectrum 640k Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2011. It uses the ZX multicolour mode.
why: A compo winner from the group that later won the same compo again with Across The Edge in 2016.

summary: Be No Sqr is a Sega Master System demo by Psidum, Sim and Slimeball, second in the Coding compo at the SMS Power Anniversary Coding Compo 2016. Psidum did the code, Sim the graphics and Slimeball the music.
why: Nominated in the That's Not Possible On This Platform category at the Meteoriks 2017.

summary: Speccy.pl's demo for the SAM Coupé, first in the 8Bit Demo compo at RetroKomp / Load Error 2015. Sir David did the code, Cat-Man the graphics and Ziutek the music, with design support from Tygrys. The video is the big-screen party showing.
why: A compo winner on the SAM Coupé.

summary: Benediction's Amstrad CPC demo, third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2012. Krusty and Eliot did the code, with graphics from Exin, CeD, Supersly and Voxfreax and music by McKlain and Dma-Sc.
why: A podium finish at Revision for the CPC, with a sizeable credit list for graphics and music.

summary: Extreme Entertainment's ZX Spectrum demo that won the Demo compo at Funtop 1998. TeeRay did the main graphics and 3D scenes, Exploder the code, rendering and camera work, and Visual the music. It features TeeRay's pictures Starin' At The Sun and Mark Anthony.
why: A compo winner whose credits list 3D scenes, rendering and camera work.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari 8-bit Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k10. The code is credited to JAC, Ooz the graphics and 505 the music.
why: A compo winner. Little else is on record, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Samar Productions' two-disk-side C64 demo that won the 8 Bit Demo compo at Intel Outside 1998.
why: One commenter calls it one of the most underrated C64 demos, and others cite the soundtrack, the pictures and the effects. A commenter notes the tunnel-vector part uses the disk drive for calculating.

quote.text: Outstanding soundtrack, some amazing pictures and crazy effects like the filled tv cube, tunnel, dot sphere, 4x4 effect zoomer etc.

summary: Trilobit's Atari VCS (2600) demo, third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2007. visy did the code and design; Ilmarque did code, graphics and music.
why: A podium finish for a two-person team on the Atari VCS. There are no comments on the sheet, so the video is the best guide.

summary: Triad's C64 demo that won the Demo compo at Floppy 2005 and was nominated for Best Demo on an Oldschool Platform at the Scene.org Awards. Iopop did the code, Twoflower the graphics and Dalezy the music.
why: Dalezy of Creators appears as a guest musician. It was reviewed in Nordic Scene Review 1 in April 2005.

summary: aTaRSi is an Atari VCS demo by Digital Sounds System, Crest and Tristar and Red Sector Inc., first in the Realtime Demo (Oldschool) compo at Nordlicht 2013. Peiselulli did the code, DeeKay the graphics and Tjoppen the music.
why: A compo winner and a three-group collaboration on the VCS. Enthusi wrote the scrolltext code.

summary: Horizon and Instinct's C64 demo, fourth in the C64 Demo compo at X 2008. JackAsser and Pernod did the code, Archmage the graphics and RaveGuru the music.
why: Sceners praise the twisters, RaveGuru's soundtrack and Archmage's pictures. The common complaint is that it's too short, and one asks what it is about.

quote.text: Very slick and enjoyable demo. Love the music and the nice gfx from Archmage.

summary: Deary is a 32K intro for the Atari 8-bit by SquoQuo, third in the Realtime Demo Size-Limited compo at Demodays 2012. Hopper did the code and 505 the music.
why: A podium finish in a size-limited compo from a two-person team.

summary: Trilobit's Atari VCS (2600) demo that won the Alternative Demo compo at Alternative Party 2008. Ilmarque did code, graphics and music; visy the engine code and design; Viznut the 3D cube part. The video calls it an 8K demo.
why: A compo winner. The 3D cube part by Viznut is the credit to watch for.

summary: Masters of Electric City's Atari 8-bit demo, second in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k12. It's tagged 128k and hires. bob_er did code and graphics, Dhor graphics and music.
why: A runner-up at Silly Venture 2k12, the same party where Lamers' Boogie Nights took first place.

summary: deMarche's ZX Spectrum 128K demo, first in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at CAFe 2019. TmK did the code, bfox the graphics, nq the music and Zeebr the direction. It uses the ZX multicolour mode, and the source is available.
why: Nominated for Best Low-End Production at the Meteoriks 2020. The video is the final version, v2, with no flicker.

summary: Stardust's ZX Spectrum demo that won the Oldschool Demo compo at Multimatograf 2024. Diver and G.D. did the graphics, sq and Kowalski the code and nq the music. The video is the final version.
why: Tagged for the Meteoriks 2025 watchlist. G.D. is credited with 3D graphics.

summary: No Pets Allowed is an Orb demo for the Commodore PET, tagged for the CBM 4032. Ultra did the code, Ilkke, Leon and Mirage the graphics, and 4mat the music and some code.
why: The video shows both the speaker and SID versions, so you can hear how the music changes between them.

summary: Oxyron's Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2013. Graham did the code, Yazoo the graphics and Booker the music, with a charset by Amarok.
why: A compo winner. Little else is on record, so the video is the best guide.

summary: The final version of Lamers' Atari 8-bit demo Prozac Dream, shown in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k17 with no placing recorded.
why: The earlier party version took second place a year before at Silly Venture 2k16. Gepard, Odyn1ec, At0m and Johny are credited with graphics, Alias, Ajcek and Szeryf with code, and XTD with the music.
